Phase 61 plan: docs/phases/framework-files-retire-what-nothing-reads.md @ 0961299 (branch phase/framework-files-retire-what-nothing-reads).

Problem: setup installs 13 framework files; 12 (templates/*.md, docs/checklists/*.md) are read by nothing except bench's is_file()-guarded checklist, and deleting them does not stick (absent -> create). Source report: docs/tagteam-issue-framework-files-no-opt-out-2026-09-20.md.

Plan departs from that report on purpose: no framework.skip key. Arbiter direction 2026-09-20 is that upgrade should clear the stale files, not add a per-project opt-out. Managed set shrinks to docs/workflows.md (+ vendored skill); the 12 paths become 'retired': provably-tagteam bytes are unlinked (the _handover precedent; bytes still ship in the package), custom copies are kept with an --accept delete line, unsupported shapes are kept not refused, emptied dirs are rmdir'd non-recursively. Bench falls back to the package checklist; needs_setup() re-keyed to docs/workflows.md; docs (data/workflows.md, README, CLAUDE.md, roadmap Getting Started) updated.

Please press on: (1) is unlink-without-recoverability sound for current/framework classifications, especially pre-manifest package-byte matches; (2) unsupported -> keep rather than refuse; (3) keeping the 8 unseeded templates in data/ as provenance; (4) anything that reads a project's templates/ or docs/checklists/ that I missed. One open question is addressed to the arbiter (automatic vs --retire flag); the plan assumes automatic.

Verified: tagteam roadmap check ok (62 phases). No code changed; suite not run (plan cycle).

The reduced managed set, bench package fallback, unsupported-retired -> keep behavior, and retaining package templates as provenance are sound. Source inspection found no additional runtime consumer of project templates/checklists beyond the bench reader and the acknowledged legacy migration backup. Automatic retirement is consistent with the recorded arbiter direction; no framework.skip or separate flag is requested.

Please resolve two migration cases in the plan before implementation:

1. Scope item 3 claims every retired preimage remains in the installed package, but _classify() accepts a matching manifest sha256 independently of the current package bytes (framework.py:322). An older, unmodified, untracked template can therefore be classified FRAMEWORK even though the installed package no longer contains its contents. A digest establishes provenance, not recovery. Distinguish package/reconstructible-rendered matches from manifest-only historical matches, and specify a recovery policy for the latter (for example, require tracked+clean recovery or save the exact preimage before automatic deletion). Add a test with historical manifest-matching bytes different from the current package and no git recovery. Retaining today's package sources alone does not cover this case.

2. Do not unconditionally drop every retired manifest entry. If unlink fails (e.g. permissions), an old manifest-only file remains on disk, but the proposed projected_manifest() forgets its only provenance. The next setup then classifies it custom and never retries automatic retirement. Preserve the prior entry for an unsuccessful retirement, following the existing refused-item behavior, and drop it after successful deletion; custom kept paths can still lose their entries as proposed. Add a two-run test: an injected unlink failure leaves the old file and provenance intact, then a successful retry retires it and removes the entry. Adjust the 'manifest lists workflows only after one run' assertion to account for refusals.

Plan review only; no tests run and no implementation files changed.
